title: Battery Management & Charging
contentStatus: Built per Content Principles (60% pass, terminology + notes). Specs confirmed per CDD - no SME dependency for this module.

sections.title: MoRo's Power System
learningObjectives: Understand why this chemistry was chosen
sections.content: All MoRo variants use LFP (Lithium Iron Phosphate) batteries, confirmed across the A-250, A-500, and A-1200. LFP chemistry is chosen for industrial applications because it's thermally stable, has a long cycle life, and tolerates frequent partial charging well - all relevant for a robot that charges opportunistically throughout a shift rather than on a single overnight cycle.

keyTerms.note: A lithium battery chemistry known for thermal stability and long cycle life, commonly used in industrial and automotive applications.

sections.title: Runtime and Charging
learningObjectives: State MoRo's confirmed runtime and charging specifications
sections.content: MoRo is rated for 8 hours of runtime and charges wirelessly in under 1 hour, consistent across all three variants. Wireless charging means MoRo docks at a charging station without a physical plug connection - it aligns with the dock and charging begins automatically. This supports opportunistic charging: a unit can top up during natural gaps in its schedule rather than requiring a dedicated, lengthy charging window.

sections.title: Charging Dock Placement and Alignment
learningObjectives: Understand the general requirement for successful wireless charging
Recognize signs of a failed or incomplete docking
sections.content: Wireless charging requires MoRo to align correctly with the charging dock - the alignment tolerance and exact docking procedure will be confirmed against DiFacto's facility guidance. Operationally, if a unit appears docked but isn't visibly charging (per its status indicator), that's worth flagging rather than assuming charging is underway.

sections.title: Extending Battery Life
learningObjectives: Understand general principles for maintaining battery health over time
Recognize operator-level habits that support battery longevity
sections.content: Like most industrial battery systems, MoRo's battery life benefits from consistent, moderate charging habits rather than repeatedly running to full depletion before charging. Taking advantage of opportunistic charging windows during a shift, rather than waiting until a unit is critically low, supports longer battery health over the unit's operational life.

sections.title: Monitoring Battery Health
learningObjectives: Understand what battery health monitoring involves at the operator level
Know the general signs worth flagging
sections.content: At this level, battery health monitoring is largely passive - watching for units that seem to deplete faster than expected, take longer than usual to charge, or show charging-related status indicators inconsistent with normal operation. Detailed diagnostic procedures for battery health belong to the technician-level curriculum (L3A); your role here is awareness and reporting.

sections.title: Low Battery Procedures
learningObjectives: Understand MoRo's general behavior when battery runs low
sections.content: MoRo is designed to manage its own low-battery state - prioritizing a return to charging before depletion becomes operationally disruptive. If you notice a unit behaving unusually and a low-battery indicator is present, treat it as context for what you're observing rather than an emergency requiring intervention beyond normal reporting.

questions.question: What battery chemistry does MoRo use?
questions.feedback: Correct. All MoRo variants use LFP batteries, confirmed across the product line.

questions.question: What is MoRo's confirmed runtime and charging time?
options: 8 hours runtime, under 1 hour wireless charging
questions.feedback: Correct. 8 hours runtime and under 1 hour wireless charging, confirmed across all variants.

questions.question: What does wireless charging mean for MoRo?
options: It never needs to be charged
It docks and charges without a physical plug connection
questions.feedback: Correct. MoRo aligns with the dock and charges automatically, no plug required.

questions.question: What charging habit supports longer battery life?
options: Always running to full depletion before charging
Consistent, moderate charging using opportunistic windows
questions.feedback: Correct. Opportunistic, moderate charging supports battery longevity over repeated full-depletion cycles.

questions.question: What is the appropriate operator-level response to a low-battery indicator with unusual behavior?
options: Treat it as context for what you're observing and report normally
questions.feedback: Correct. Low battery is useful context, not an emergency requiring intervention beyond standard reporting.
